def transaction_frames(initial: dict[str, int], commands: list[tuple]) -> tuple[dict, list[bool]]:
    """Process ('begin',), ('commit',), ('rollback',), and ('move',src,dst,amount). Initial balances are nonnegative exact ints (bool invalid), account names strings. Amounts are nonnegative exact ints. Both accounts must exist, even for amount zero. Validate every command including ones inside failed frames. Invalid input, unbalanced frames, or commit/rollback without begin raises ValueError. Move from an account to itself always succeeds without a balance check. An overdraft outside a frame is ignored. Inside a frame it marks ONLY that innermost frame failed; ignore subsequent moves there. Begin within a failed frame raises ValueError. On commit, apply a successful frame to its parent; failed frames discard changes without failing their parent. Rollback always discards. Return final balances and one boolean per commit in processing order (true iff committed frame succeeded). Never mutate inputs."""

def escaped_records(text: str) -> list[list[str]]:
    """Parse records separated by LF and fields by |. Backslash escapes exactly backslash, |, double quote, or n (n becomes LF); any other escape or dangling backslash is invalid. A quoted field begins only with a double quote at field start, ends with an unescaped double quote, and must then be immediately followed by |, LF, or end. Inside quotes, actual LF and | are data. A double quote in an unquoted field is invalid. Empty input yields []; otherwise empty fields and empty records are preserved, except ONE final record delimiter LF does not create an additional record. CR is ordinary data; Unicode is unchanged. Unclosed quotes or bad escapes raise ValueError. Return decoded fields."""

def capped_apportion(total: int, weights: list[int], caps: list[int], groups: list[str] | None = None) -> list[int]:
    """Allocate exact integer total by iterative capped largest remainders. All inputs are exact ints (bool invalid), nonnegative, lists equal length. Zero-weight bins never receive units even if they have capacity. If eligible capacity is less than total, raise ValueError. Start allocations at zero. Each round considers bins with positive weight and remaining capacity; compute exact ideal shares of the remaining total proportional to their weights. If any ideal share >= that bin's remaining capacity, simultaneously fill ALL such bins to capacity and restart (allocate nothing to the others in that round). Otherwise give each bin floor(ideal), then leftover single units by descending fractional remainder, ties by ORIGINAL index. Stop when allocated total; total zero returns zeros but still validates everything. Do not mutate inputs. Arbitrarily large integers must remain exact. If groups is supplied, require equal-length string labels. Allocate in TWO levels: group order is first appearance, group weight is sum of ALL member weights (including positive-weight zero-capacity members), group capacity is sum of capacities of positive-weight members only. Apply the same capped-round algorithm to group totals first, then independently to each group's bins, with original-index ties inside groups. All validation still applies before any allocation."""

def wall_occurrences(start, stop, hour: int, minute: int) -> list:
    """Inputs start/stop are aware datetimes sharing the identical ZoneInfo tzinfo object. Validate hour/minute as exact ints within 0..23 / 0..59, including empty ranges; otherwise ValueError. Reject naive inputs, non-ZoneInfo zones, distinct zone objects, reversed UTC instants. Return every instant in [start,stop) whose local wall time equals hour:minute:00.000000, chronological by UTC. Enumerate inclusive local dates from start's local date through stop's local date; nonexistent wall times during forward jumps yield none. Ambiguous times during backward jumps yield BOTH instants, deduplicated by UTC. Never mutate inputs. Returned datetimes use the original zone object and correct fold. Do not compare same-zone aware datetimes by their wall-time ordering."""

def patch_spans(text: str, edits: list[tuple[int, int, str]]) -> str:
    """All edit coordinates are Unicode code point offsets in ORIGINAL text. Each (start,end,replacement) requires exact integer endpoints (bool invalid), 0<=start<=end<=len(text), and replacement string; malformed edits raise ValueError. Positive-width intervals must not overlap. Zero-width insertions may be at either endpoint of a replacement, but strictly inside one is invalid. Multiple insertions at a coordinate concatenate in input order, even when separated in input by other edits. At a replacement's start, emit all insertions BEFORE its replacement; at its end, emit insertions after it. Adjacent replacements allowed. Return simultaneously edited text; don't mutate edits. Validation must include all edits, not only ones reached during reconstruction."""

def ttl_lru(capacity: int, actions: list[tuple]) -> tuple[list, list]:
    """Simulate a TTL LRU cache. Capacity nonnegative exact int, bool invalid. Actions are ('put',time,key,value,ttl) or ('get',time,key), with exact nonnegative integer time/ttl, string keys, times nondecreasing. Invalid input raises ValueError. Before EACH action remove entries with expiry <= time. Put replaces an existing value, refreshes expiry=time+ttl and makes most recent; evict least recent while over capacity. A ttl=0 put removes an existing same-key entry but must not evict any other key. Get returns value or None; hit promotes to most recent without refreshing TTL. Return (get results, surviving (key,value,expiry) triples from least to most recent) after the LAST action; no further expiry. Validate even when capacity zero. Values can be None. Don't mutate actions. Additionally support nested ('begin',time), ('commit',time), ('rollback',time) transaction actions. Begin snapshots current cache content, LRU order and absolute expiries after that action's normal pre-expiry. Commit keeps current cache; rollback restores the snapshot THEN IMMEDIATELY removes entries expired at rollback time. Time never rolls back; observed get results never roll back. Unbalanced transactions or commit/rollback without begin raises ValueError. Put/get semantics, final order and all time validation remain unchanged."""

def nested_expansion(text: str, limit: int) -> str:
    """Parse a repetition language over Unicode code points. Syntax: decimal ASCII count immediately followed by [body] repeats body count times; nested repeats permitted. Counts may have leading zeros. Unescaped ASCII digits are ONLY counts, never literals; require following [. Unescaped ] closes a repetition; an unescaped [ without count is invalid. Backslash quotes ANY next character literally, including digits/brackets/backslash; dangling escape invalid. Other characters, including non-ASCII digits, are literal. limit is a nonnegative exact int (bool invalid). Invalid syntax or final expanded length > limit raises ValueError. A zero repetition validates its body's syntax but does NOT apply limit to intermediate body expansion; e.g. 0[999999999999999999999[a]] with limit=0 returns ''. Never allocate output exceeding limit while evaluating a discarded zero-repeat subtree. Empty text returns ''. A repetition may additionally have ONE suffix {start:stop}, slicing its FULL repeated output by Python code-point slice semantics, with omitted bounds and signed ASCII decimal integers permitted (no step). Unescaped braces are reserved and invalid elsewhere. Limits apply ONLY to final output, never intermediates: 999999999999999999999[a]{-2:} yields 'aa' at limit 2; discarded or sliced huge repeats must not be allocated. Validate all syntax even in unused portions. Counts/bounds may have thousands of digits and must not hit Python's decimal int-string safety limit."""

def ragged_walk(rows: list[list[int]]) -> list[int]:
    """Every existing (row,column) cell is traversable, including empty rows and ragged widths. Start at lexicographically smallest cell, facing right. Emit its value and mark visited. From each cell try moving one cell in current direction; if unavailable/visited rotate clockwise (right, down, left, up), trying all four. Take first valid move and retain that direction. If no adjacent unvisited cell exists, jump to lexicographically smallest remaining cell and RESET direction to right. Continue until every cell emitted exactly once. Empty grid returns []. This is a wall-following traversal with disconnected restarts, not concentric rectangular rings. Return values, preserve rows."""

def dependency_waves(deps: dict[str, list[str]], cancelled: set[str], width: int, capacities: dict[str, int] | None = None, demands: dict[str, dict[str, int]] | None = None) -> list[list[str]]:
    """Names are arbitrary strings; dependency lists contain names in deps. Unknown dependencies/cancelled names or nonpositive/non-exact-int width (bool invalid) raises ValueError. First remove cancelled nodes AND transitively every node depending on a removed node; this cancellation propagates even through cycles. Schedule remaining nodes in waves of at most width, selecting lexicographically smallest ready names. A node becomes ready only in a wave AFTER all its dependencies were scheduled, never later within the same wave. Ignore duplicate dependencies. If the remaining graph contains a cycle, raise ValueError (no partial result). Validate unknown dependencies even in removed nodes. Return waves; no mutation. Optional resource mode: capacities and demands must be supplied together. Capacities map string resource names to nonnegative exact ints; demands map known node names to dictionaries of known resource names and nonnegative exact ints. Missing demand means zero. Validate even cancelled nodes. Among ready nodes choose a feasible subset of at most width with MAXIMUM cardinality, then lexicographically smallest sorted node tuple, subject to sums of demands <= each capacity. A node too large to fit a wave causes ValueError only if not removed. No within-wave dependency activation. At most 18 ready nodes need be handled."""

def significant_round(value: str, digits: int, divisor: str = "1") -> str:
    """Round a finite Decimal-compatible numeric string to digits significant decimal digits using exact ties-to-even, independent of ambient Decimal context precision/rounding. digits is a positive exact int (bool invalid). Invalid/nonfinite numbers or digits raise ValueError. Return a plain decimal string with no exponent, trim insignificant fractional trailing zeros and the dot, retain integer zeros, normalize ANY signed zero to '0'. Scientific notation and whitespace accepted like Decimal. Integers and exponents may exceed 1000 digits in size; do not convert through float. Carry may increase digit count. Do not change ambient context. Round the EXACT rational quotient value/divisor, never a finitely approximated intermediate quotient. Divisor is a finite NONZERO Decimal-compatible numeric string; validate it even for zero value. Nonterminating quotients supported. Preserve original significant-digit, ties-to-even and plain-output rules. Coefficients may exceed Python's decimal int-string safety limit, and exponents may have magnitude 5000; no global int-string-limit or Decimal-context changes."""

def escaped_glob(pattern: str, text: str, capture: bool = False):
    """Match ENTIRE text by code point: * matches zero or more arbitrary characters (including LF), ? matches exactly one, backslash escapes any next character. Classes [abc], [!abc] (negated only for unescaped ! first), and ranges [a-z] are supported. Inside a class, backslash quotes any character; unescaped ] always closes, so literal ] requires escaping. Unescaped - denotes range ONLY when between two class atoms; at first/last position it is literal. Reject empty classes, descending ranges, unclosed classes, dangling backslashes, or consecutive range operators like [a-b-c] with ValueError. Outside classes ] is literal. Validate the WHOLE pattern even when an earlier prefix cannot match. Unicode comparisons/ranges use ord; no normalization. Do not use platform pathname-glob semantics. capture must be exact bool. If true return None for no full match; otherwise a list of (start,end) text offsets, one for EVERY unescaped * outside classes in pattern order, including adjacent stars and zero-length spans. Among matches choose lexicographically smallest tuple of captured lengths (leftmost star as short as possible first). A matching pattern with no stars returns []. Do not collapse adjacent stars. Full eager pattern validation still applies."""

def rational_expression(source: str, bindings: dict | None = None, symbolic: bool = False):
    """Evaluate a complete expression as fractions.Fraction using ASCII integer tokens, parentheses, operators + - * / ** and unary + -. Whitespace is ONLY space, tab, CR, LF; it may separate tokens but never join digits into one token. Grammar (highest to lowest): power := atom ['**' unary]; unary := ('+'|'-') unary | power; product := unary {('*'|'/') unary}; sum := product {('+'|'-') product}; atom := integer | '(' sum ')'. Thus exponentiation is right-associative and binds more tightly than unary minus on its LEFT, but allows unary minus on its RIGHT. Exponent must evaluate to an integer; negative exponents allowed. Treat 0**0 as 1. Invalid syntax, noninteger exponent, division by zero, or zero to negative power raises ValueError. Reject Unicode digits and unsupported operators. No eval/exec or float conversion. If bindings is supplied (including {}), extend tokens with ASCII identifiers and commas; bound values must be exact int (bool invalid) or Fraction, and keys valid ASCII identifiers. Enable functions abs(x), min(x,y), max(x,y), ifzero(test,when_zero,otherwise). ifzero evaluates ONLY the selected branch but validates syntax, function arity and all variable names in both branches; arithmetic errors/noninteger exponents in the unused branch are ignored. Undefined variables or malformed bindings raise ValueError even if unused. No eval/exec. symbolic must be exact bool. If true, parse arithmetic expressions with variable x and other ASCII identifiers supplied in bindings (None means {}). No function calls in this mode. Return (numerator_coefficients, denominator_coefficients) as nonempty tuples of Fraction in ASCENDING degree, trailing zeros removed. Reduce polynomial common factors by exact gcd and normalize denominator to MONIC. Zero is ((Fraction(0),),(Fraction(1),)). Exponents must simplify to an integer constant rational function; positive/negative integer powers allowed, zero denominator or nonconstant/noninteger exponent raises ValueError. Division can cancel algebraically, e.g. (x*x-1)/(x-1) reduces to x+1. Inputs have intermediate polynomial degree <=16. Other modes retain previous semantics, and all bindings still validate."""

def priority_overlay(intervals: list[tuple], closed: bool = False) -> list[tuple]:
    """Each (start,end,priority,label) covers [start,end); endpoints are int/float excluding bool and NaN, infinities permitted, start<=end; priority exact int (bool invalid), label string. Invalid items raise ValueError including zero-width intervals. For each covered point select interval of greatest priority; ties by LATEST input index. Return sorted maximal nonempty segments (start,end,label). Adjacent selected segments with equal labels merge even when winner changes; never bridge an uncovered gap. Zero-width intervals do not cover points. Output endpoint infinities preserved. Do not mutate intervals; no arithmetic midpoint calculations (infinite or adjacent float endpoints can defeat them). closed must be exact bool. If true, each input instead has six fields (start,end,priority,label,left_closed,right_closed), both flags exact bool. Work on FINITE real points: infinite endpoints are never included. Zero-width finite intervals cover a singleton iff both flags true. Return maximal connected segments as (start,end,label,left_closed,right_closed), including singleton points. Same winner/last-index and label-merge rules; equal-label open intervals separated by an uncovered endpoint must NOT merge. All validation applies even to empty intervals."""

def prefix_cents(amounts: list[str]) -> list[int]:
    """Parse finite Decimal-compatible signed amount strings. Return integer cent adjustments per row such that their cumulative sum after EACH prefix equals the EXACT prefix sum rounded to cents, ties-to-even. This is cumulative balancing, not independently rounded rows. Negative amounts allowed, any invalid/nonfinite input raises ValueError, including late inputs. Context precision/rounding must not affect results or be mutated. No float conversion. Support coefficients longer than 1000 decimal digits and exponents within +/-2000. Empty list returns []; don't mutate inputs."""

def utf8_rechunk(parts: list[bytes], budget: int, encoding: str = "utf8") -> list[bytes]:
    """Parts concatenate to a UTF-8 byte stream; part boundaries may split any code point. Validate STRICT Unicode UTF-8 (reject overlong, surrogate, invalid continuation, truncated sequences). budget is positive exact int (bool invalid). Return greedy longest-prefix chunks of at most budget BYTES, never splitting a code point. If any code point takes more bytes than budget, raise ValueError. Empty stream returns [], no empty output chunks. Preserve bytes exactly (including UTF-8 BOM as a normal code point), no Unicode normalization. All parts must be bytes, not bytearray. Invalid input raises ValueError, including invalid tails after a too-long code point. Do not mutate parts. encoding must be 'utf8' or 'utf16'. In utf16 mode, a nonempty concatenated stream MUST begin with either UTF-16 BOM, determining endian order. Decode strict UTF-16 including that initial BOM as U+FEFF data; reject malformed/unpaired surrogates, odd byte counts or missing BOM. Greedy byte chunks must keep supplementary code points' surrogate pairs together and preserve ALL input bytes exactly. Keep the initial BOM only where it already occurs; never add a BOM to subsequent chunks. budget still counts BYTES. Empty stream returns [] in either mode. Other modes raise ValueError."""

def folded_spans(text: str, needle: str, ignore_marks: bool = False) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
    """Split text into units: each code point with combining class zero starts a new unit and absorbs all following nonzero-combining-class code points; a leading run of nonzero-combining characters is ONE unit. Fold each unit separately as NFC(unit).casefold(), concatenating to a folded stream. Fold needle with the SAME unit procedure. Return distinct original (start,end) offsets of matches ONLY when BOTH folded endpoints coincide with text UNIT boundaries. Find overlapping matches; sort by start then end. Empty folded needle yields [] (no empty matches). No matching through a partial expansion: 's' does not match 'ß' but 'ss' does. Code point offsets, not bytes/grapheme-library boundaries; normalization does not reorder across units. Do not mutate inputs. ignore_marks must be exact bool. If true, after each unit's original NFC+casefold transformation, apply NFD, drop characters with NONZERO combining class, then NFC again. Apply this also to needle. Empty transformed units remain valid original boundaries: return ALL distinct original boundary pairs whose folded spans match, including optional empty units before/after a match. Empty folded needle still returns []."""

def lease_trace(events: list[tuple]) -> tuple[list, dict]:
    """Process ('acquire',time,key,owner,ttl), ('renew',time,key,owner,token,ttl), ('release',time,key,owner,token). Times/ttl are nonnegative exact ints, tokens positive exact ints, bool invalid; key/owner strings. Times nondecreasing; malformed events raise ValueError. Before each event expire all leases with expiry<=time. Acquiring a held key always fails (even same owner) returning None; free acquire assigns next GLOBAL monotonically increasing token starting 1 and returns token. ttl=0 acquire still succeeds and CONSUMES token but retains no lease. Renew succeeds iff key matches owner and token, returns boolean, sets expiry=time+ttl (ttl=0 removes); failure false. Release likewise returns boolean and removes only on match. Return result for EACH event plus surviving key -> (owner,token,expiry). No concurrency, no input mutation."""

def coupon_route(edges: list[tuple[str, str, int]], start: str, end: str, hops: int, required: tuple[str, ...] = (), discounts: int = 1):
    """Directed edges have nonnegative exact integer costs; hops is a nonnegative exact integer; bool invalid. Names strings. Invalid edges raise ValueError even if unreachable or start==end. Find cheapest walk from start to end using AT MOST hops edges; nodes/edges may repeat, parallel edges allowed. You MAY discount at most ONE traversed edge to floor(cost/2), including zero-cost edges. Return (minimum cost, tuple of node names) or None if unreachable. Ties by FEWEST edges, then lexicographically smallest entire node tuple. Start==end admits empty walk with cost 0. Do not mutate edges. Discount is optional; no final flag required. Costs arbitrary size integers. Extend with a required node-name tuple that must occur as an ordered subsequence of path positions, including start/end. ONE path position satisfies at most ONE requirement, even repeated names. May pass through end and leave before final arrival. discounts is a nonnegative exact int (bool invalid), allowing up to that many half-price edges, but two discounted edges must NEVER be consecutive. Requirements must be strings; names absent from graph simply make route impossible. Same cost/fewest edges/full tuple tie rules. Validate everything even for the empty walk."""

def revision_log(events: list[tuple]) -> list[tuple]:
    """Input events (id,revision,operation,key,value) have id/key strings, revision nonnegative exact int (bool invalid), operation 'set' or 'delete'. Value arbitrary. Validate EVERY event before choosing winners. For EACH id retain only highest revision; equal-revision ties use LATEST input position. Replay retained events in order of their WINNING input positions, not first appearance/revision/id. Maintain insertion ordered mapping: set new key appends; set existing changes value WITHOUT moving; delete absent ignored; delete then set re-appends. Return list of (key,value) in final mapping order, with fresh DEEP COPIES of values so modifying return doesn't mutate input; don't mutate events. Empty input []. Also allow operation 'undo': its key is the ID of a retained non-undo event to disable; value is ignored. Select revision winners first, then each retained undo must target a strictly earlier retained non-undo event (unknown, forward or undo targets raise ValueError). Repeated undo of one target is harmless. Loser undo events need only structural validation, not target resolution. Final mapping must equal replay of retained ordinary events with ALL disabled events omitted, including insertion order consequences of omitted deletes. Deep-copy/mutation rules remain unchanged."""

def indented_records(source: str) -> list[dict]:
    """Parse a forest of lines each containing one JSON STRING label with optional trailing whitespace and # comment. Blank lines and lines whose first non-indentation char is # ignored and don't affect nesting. Indentation uses spaces and tabs; a tab advances to next multiple of FOUR columns, starting at zero. Nonblank data lines must have indent a nonnegative multiple of TWO. First/root data lines must indent zero; child indent must be exactly parent+2; dedent must match a previously open level. JSON string may contain # and escaped quotes. Require only space/tab after closing string before optional # comment; reject nonstring JSON, invalid escapes, garbage after string, invalid indentation, or skipped levels with ValueError. Split lines ONLY at LF; remove one terminal CR per line for CRLF. Return nodes {'label':decoded_label,'children':[nodes]}; no external libraries."""
